chains.title: PKNOX1 preferentially binds C and may alter RFX6 regulation
chains.element: The variant lies in the enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2496909; activity of this element in LNCaP is not established.

links.claim: PKNOX1 is the expressed, modelled TF with a reported variant-overlapping peak, and its QBiC-SELEX model predicts stronger binding to C; however, the peak is from HEK293T, the predicted site is weak, and neither result establishes PKNOX1 occupancy at this base in LNCaP.
The variant overlaps enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2496909, but the available biosample-maximum scores do not establish activity in LNCaP.

RFX6 is a candidate target because the variant is intronic to RFX6 and prostate-cancer credible sets prioritize it, although neither a direct cCRE-to-RFX6 link nor a significant prostate RFX6 eQTL is shown.
This is a candidate mechanism in LNCaP-like cells, where PKNOX1 is expressed, but ENCODE reports no matching-biosample peak over the variant.

A PKNOX1-dependent effect on RFX6 could contribute to prostate-cancer risk, but the locus association and RFX6 literature do not establish this specific causal chain or the direction of its regulatory effect.

predictions: If PKNOX1 mediates an effect at this base in prostate cells, C will show greater PKNOX1 occupancy than T, and disrupting PKNOX1 or its local binding site will reduce the allele-dependent effect.
The predicted binding difference alone does not specify whether RFX6 expression rises or falls.
falsified_if: A sensitive allele-resolved assay in relevant prostate cells detects no PKNOX1 occupancy difference between C and T, and PKNOX1 perturbation does not alter any variant-dependent molecular effect.

Dysregulated expression or mutations of the RFX6 gene in prostate cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, gastric cancer, melanoma, and other tumors have garnered significant interest, with studies showing that such alterations affect tumor cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, and are correlated with an unfavorable clinical prognosis in patients carrying RFX6 mutations.

Here the FinnGen cohort phenome-wide analysis, along with multiple genome-wide association studies, has consistently identified the rs[masked]-RFX6/6q22 locus associated with prostate cancer (PCa) risk across diverse populations.

Mechanistically, RFX6 upregulates HOXA10 that profoundly correlates with adverse PCa outcomes and is pivotal in RFX6-mediated PCa progression, facilitating the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and modulating the TGFβ/SMAD signaling axis.
